title: PbfuzzSettings
description: Settings namespace `pbfuzz` — pbfuzz's OWN behaviour, edited in the DSH web settings card. Nothing about the target project appears here; that all lives in the campaign. W1 turns this into the schemastery `Config` it hands to `settings.installSection`, and W6 renders the card from the same schema. Enforcement runs in-process (a native `ctx.tools.guard()` inside the host plugin), so there is no settings snapshot file for a separate process to read.

tools.description: Which auxiliary analysis tools are enabled. A tool enabled here is exercised for real by the startup self-check; a tool disabled here has its pbfuzz tools hidden by `ctx.tools.restrict()` and denied by the `phase_gate` hook.

staticAnalysis.description: Static analysis provider. `kanalyzer` is selectable only when the dsh-kanalyzer plugin is installed; the card greys the option out with an install hint otherwise.

deviationDetection.description: Needs static analysis for critical-BB mode; degrades to target-only without it.

interactiveDebug.description: Allow the agent an interactive debugger through DSH's `terminal`, replacing the old gdb FIFO MCP server.

budget.description: How long one campaign may run. A native PIER driver (`agent/turn-stopping` + `ctx.jobs.onJobDone`) advances the loop unattended, so these three caps are the ONLY brakes on an unattended run — they must actually stop it (writing `phase: STOPPED`), not merely stop nudging it.

maxPierRounds.description: PLAN→REFLECT cycles allowed. On reaching it, the campaign guard denies REFLECT→PLAN and `pbfuzz_reflect` writes STOPPED instead.

autoContinue.description: Whether the PIER driver steers a natural turn-stop back into the loop while the campaign is active, not yet at a terminal phase, and not waiting on the user or a running fuzz job.

maxConsecutiveForcedContinues.description: DSH's own turn-stopping seam has no loop cap of its own, so the driver limits itself: after this many consecutive forced continuations in the same phase/round it stops steering. In headless mode (no user can re-arm it) it writes STOPPED instead of merely giving up; in an interactive session it just lets the turn end, and any user message resets the counter.

stage1MinConcreteParams.description: Minimum concrete batch-plan entries before the sampler takes over, so stage 1 actually tests the hypothesis.

enableDebuggerForAll.description: Trace every iteration rather than only stage-1 concrete runs. Correct but slow.

interviewPolicy.description: `when-missing` asks only what the agent could not infer — the default that keeps onboarding cheap. `never` is the headless mode: a missing required field is an error, not a question.

deriveTargetFrom.description: Which bug-information forms the agent may derive a target location from.

confirmTimeoutMin.description: Minutes to wait for a human to answer the campaign-review (Approve/Revise) panel before `pbfuzz_campaign confirm` gives up with an error the agent can recover from. `0` (the default) waits indefinitely, the idiomatic DSH behaviour; set a bound for unattended/monitored deployments so a session cannot idle forever on an absent human.

oracleDefaults.description: Defaults the questionnaire proposes; a campaign may override them.

pythonPath.description: Interpreter for the engine sidecar. Changing it restarts the sidecar.

generatorMemLimitMB.description: Generators are model-written code; they run in a subprocess under rlimit, never in-process.

fuzzBackground.description: Run `pbfuzz_fuzz` as a `ctx.jobs` background job. A headless run (`onboarding.interviewPolicy: never` / `/pbfuzz run`) always runs it in the foreground instead, regardless of this setting — a one-shot headless process exits as soon as its turn goes idle and would kill a background fuzz job before it finishes.

guards.description: In-process enforcement (a native `ctx.tools.guard()` in the host plugin) governing state writes, phase legality and shell commands that would tamper with campaign state.

bashGuard.description: Deny shell commands that would edit state files or metrics behind the guard's back.

hideToolsWithoutCampaign.description: Keep the pbfuzz tools out of the model's tool list until a confirmed campaign exists. Off by default: the visible set is otherwise constant for a whole session, and every change to it costs the model's prompt prefix cache.

status.description: Read-only in the card; written by the host after `/pbfuzz selfcheck` runs the environment self-check (engine ping, python/contracts version, sandbox round trip, static-analysis/tracer availability). Cached with a TTL so a campaign start reads this instead of re-running it on the critical path.
